High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:166583
Court No. - 70

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36175 of 2023
Applicant :- Somwati

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Jitendra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Jitendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 121 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Civil Lines,
District Rampur during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 02.04.2023 against applicant and her family members including husband of the deceased and according to the FIR marriage of the deceased was performed with the son of the applicant on 04.11.2022 and after marriage applicant and her family members tortured her for demand of Rs. 5 lakhs and when on 31.03.2023 after receiving information, informant arrived then found that after admitting his sister i.e. deceased in the hospital, applicant and her family members had gone and thereafter applicant and her family members refused to take her back, therefore, informant had to take her in his home and in spite of best medical treatment she died on 01.04.2023.
Somwati vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99520386/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and entire allegation of demand of dowry made against her is totally false and baseless and actually her daughter-in-law accidentally slipped from the stairs and sustained injuries and applicant and her family members admitted her in the hospital and this fact is admitted in the FIR itself but after receiving information, informant arrived at the hospital and has taken the deceased with him and deceased died in her paternal home and subsequently totally on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
He further submits that applicant is lady and in the present matter she is in jail since 28.04.2023.
5. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Although, from the record it reflects that daughter-in-law of the applicant died due to ante mortem head injury within seven years of her marriage but admittedly she died in her paternal home and from the record it reflects that deceased was admitted in the hospital by the applicant and her family members.

8. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
9. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant - Somwati be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
